input.summary: Two distinct, now-proven failure causes on venice/repo-requirements-audit-v1. Run 42553625095 (head 653d099, job 128954439178, 12s) failed at step 5 'Build matrices from authority files' with exit code 1 and skipped tests and commit; run 42553597443 (head 4a4a8ba, job 128954318362, 11s) passed both 'Build matrices' and 'Run source-matched tests' and failed only at step 7 'Commit regenerated matrices' with exit code 1. The second case is the empty-diff commit, since the regenerated matrices are unchanged and the step has nothing to commit. The first case is a Python syntax error in the build_gantt.py I wrote: its header is a multi-line single-quoted string instead of a docstring, so importing it from build_matrices.py raises SyntaxError. This turn fixes that docstring quoting and reads the workflow to patch the commit guard.
input.next: Read .github/workflows/venice-repo-requirements-audit.yml to see the exact 'Commit regenerated matrices' shell, then edit the step so a clean tree exits 0 (git diff --quiet guard that skips commit and push) and push the workflow edit, then confirm the resulting run on venice/repo-requirements-audit-v1 is green with build, pytest and commit steps all success.

contribution.description: Localized both red runs to exact steps: 42553625095 fails in 'Build matrices from authority files' (exit 1, tests and commit skipped), which is the SyntaxError from build_gantt.py's single-quoted multi-line header being imported by build_matrices; 42553597443 passes build and tests and fails only in 'Commit regenerated matrices', which is an unconditional commit on a clean tree. Two separate defects, each now tied to a named failing step rather than guessed.

pitfalls.problem: build_gantt.py opened with a single-quoted multi-line string, so importing it from build_matrices.py raised SyntaxError and the 'Build matrices from authority files' step exited 1 (run 42553625095).
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trusting the write_file ok=true receipt as proof the Python source parses; the receipt proves the blob landed, not that it is valid Python.
pitfalls.lesson: Any new module that build_matrices imports must be validated by the workflow's build step before being wired in; check the build step's conclusion, not just the write receipt.

pitfalls.problem: 'Commit regenerated matrices' exits 1 when regeneration produces no diff, failing an otherwise green build+test run (42553597443 at 4a4a8ba).
pitfalls.failed_approach: Assuming the step is already diff-guarded because its intent is to commit only on change.
pitfalls.lesson: A regeneration-and-commit step must branch on git diff --quiet and exit 0 on a clean tree; verify by the step conclusion on a run whose matrices are unchanged.
